title: Create a memorable abstract brand symbol and logo for BossDiodov
proj_desc:
IMPORTANT BEFORE APPLYING
Please do not send a generic AI-generated proposal, AI-written analysis, or automatically generated logo concepts.
I already have paid access to AI tools. I am hiring for your own design thinking, taste, judgement and ability to create a strong original symbol. A short personal proposal in your own words is more valuable than a long generic response.
AI may support private research or ideation, but the final logo must be your own original, deliberately constructed vector design.
PROJECT
I need a distinctive standalone symbol and matching logo for BossDiodov, a company specialising in professional LED lighting systems, installation and technical solutions.
The priority is the symbol, not simply styling the company name. I want a mark that can eventually represent the brand without the word BossDiodov beside it.
It does not need to literally represent lighting, LEDs or electricity. I prefer a simple, memorable abstract symbol with a strong shape and no obvious literal meaning.
WHAT I LIKE
- Simple, distinctive symbols that are easy to recognise and remember.
- A mark that works independently from the name.
- Strong black-and-white performance and good readability at small sizes.
- Suitable for favicon, social avatar, workwear, stickers, vehicles and print.
- A shape strong enough to work without glow, gradients, 3D effects or presentation mockups.
I can provide references to explain the principle I like, but they must not be copied.
WHAT I DO NOT WANT
Please avoid generic clichés such as LED strips, light bulbs, lightning bolts, plugs, power buttons, electrical icons, glowing letters or stock-style technology logos.
Do not force the symbol into the letter B unless there is a genuinely strong concept behind it.
No stock logos, templates, recycled client work or pre-existing symbols.
THREE-STAGE PROCESS
Stage 1 — Independent thinking
I will explain the company, audience and desired brand qualities, but I will intentionally withhold my own symbol ideas and sketches.
Please create 3 genuinely different conceptual directions, not minor variations of one icon, with a short explanation behind each.
Stage 2 — Directed exploration
I will give one consolidated round of detailed feedback.
If one direction is promising, we develop it. If none works, I will share additional references and my own ideas.
This stage includes up to 2 new or substantially reworked directions if needed.
Stage 3 — Refinement
We select the strongest direction and refine proportions, geometry, typography, spacing, colour, symbol/wordmark relationship and small-size performance.
This is the final refinement stage, not another full concept search.
FINAL DELIVERABLES
- Primary BossDiodov logo.
- Standalone symbol / brand mark.
- Horizontal and compact versions where appropriate.
- Black, white/reversed and colour versions if relevant.
- SVG, editable vector source (AI/EPS or equivalent), PDF and transparent PNG.
- Favicon/avatar-ready version.
- Colour values and recommended typefaces.
- Disclosure of any font or third-party licence costs before approval.
No business cards, social templates, stationery or full brand book are required.
ORIGINALITY AND RIGHTS
The final artwork must be original and created for this project.
After final payment, I require commercial usage rights and transfer of the relevant IP rights to the approved final artwork.
Any third-party assets or licensing restrictions must be disclosed in advance.
YOUR PROPOSAL
I will personally review your PeoplePerHour portfolio. Please make sure it contains relevant examples of original logo marks and brand symbols.
Do not create free speculative work for this proposal.
Please send a short personal response explaining:
- why your experience fits this project;
- that you accept the complete 3-stage process;
- that your fixed fee is USD 110 for the entire project;
- your realistic timeframe;
- any questions you need answered before starting.
I will choose based on portfolio quality, symbol design, typography, design thinking, communication and understanding of the goal.
BUDGET AND PAYMENT
Fixed design fee: USD 110 for the complete project, not per stage or per concept.
Preferred timeframe: approximately 1–2 weeks.
Remote project. No preferred designer location.
All payments must go through PeoplePerHour using its escrow process. No direct or off-platform payments.
Before starting, we will confirm scope, stages, schedule, deliverables and any payment checkpoints in the PeoplePerHour WorkStream. Any staged payments must remain within the total USD 110 fee.

title: Drupal Developer Needed – Image Styles Causing High Disk Usage
proj_desc:
We are looking for an experienced Drupal developer to investigate and fix excessive disk usage caused by generated image derivatives.

Our `sites/default/files/styles` directory contains **20,000+ images** and keeps growing. The website uses Drupal Feeds, Image Styles, ImageAPI Optimize/WebP, Drush queues, and cron jobs.

Tasks:
- Identify why so many image derivatives are continuously generated.
- Review Drupal Image Styles and remove/optimize unnecessary styles.
- Review Feeds/import processes and image processing.
- Check ImageAPI Optimize/WebP configuration.
- Safely clean up unnecessary existing derivatives.
- Implement an automatic cleanup/retention solution.
- Review relevant cron/Drush queue jobs.
- Prevent disk usage from continuously increasing.

Important:
We do not want a cron job that blindly deletes the entire `styles` directory. The solution must be Drupal-aware and must not cause broken images or unnecessary regeneration.

Please explain your proposed approach and provide examples of similar Drupal performance/storage issues you have solved.



WHAT WE DISCOVERED UNTILL NOW:
We also traced the image_api_optimize_* files to the Drupal ImageAPI Optimize module. Its configuration confirms that the module is enabled and that the wimage pipeline uses the WebP processor at quality 70:

status: true
name: wimage
label: Wimage

processors:
id: webp_webp
data:
quality: 70

The Drupal configuration also shows that the news_feed_image style uses this image optimization pipeline:

config/sync/image.style.news_feed_image.yml:
pipeline: wimage

proj_desc:

## Project Scope

The integration should cover:

- Connect our existing CMS/backend with Shopify

Your job will be to go through the footage, find the interesting moments yourself, and turn them into approximately 14 short-form videos per week.

I DON’T want to have to provide a detailed brief for every Reel.

I’m looking for someone who understands social media and can look at raw footage and think:

* “This would make a good POV video.”
* “There’s a story here.”
* “This could work with a current trend.”
* “We could show the BTS followed by the finished result.”
* “This could become a filmmaking tip.”
* “This moment is funny/interesting enough to make content from.”

Types of Content

The content could include:

* POV / “day in the life” videos
* Behind-the-scenes property shoots
* BTS → final result videos
* Videography/filmmaking tips
* Trending Instagram/TikTok concepts
* Funny or interesting moments from shoots
* Cinematic BTS edits
* Story-led mini-vlogs
* Gear/filmmaking content
* Working with estate agents/clients
* My journey building a videography business
* Simple talking/BTS clips with strong hooks, captions and music

Not every video needs complicated editing. Some may be very simple 10–20 second Reels, while others can be more developed.

What I’m Looking For

You should:

* Have experience editing Instagram Reels, TikToks or YouTube Shorts
* Understand hooks, pacing, captions and retention
* Keep up with current short-form trends
* Be comfortable finding content within larger amounts of raw footage
* Be able to suggest your own concepts
* Understand modern, clean editing
* Have good communication
* Be interested in working together long-term

Experience with filmmaking, videography or real-estate content is a bonus.

Volume & Budget

Approximately 14 short-form videos per week

Budget: £50 GBP per week

This is intended to be consistent, long-term weekly work for the right editor.

Initially, we’ll do a paid trial period to make sure we’re a good fit. If the personal brand grows and the workload increases, there will be opportunities for the role and budget to grow as well.

To Apply

Please send:

1. Examples of short-form content you’ve edited.
2. Your Instagram/TikTok editing experience.
3. What software you use.
4. Your timezone/country.
5. Confirmation that you’re happy with £50/week for approximately 14 videos.
6. Most importantly: give me 3 Reel ideas you would create for a 19-year-old videographer filming luxury/property content around the UK.

Please start your application with the word “CAMERA” so I know you’ve actually read the full job description.

I’m not looking for someone to simply cut clips together.

I’m looking for an editor who can help me turn what I’m already doing every week into entertaining content and build a personal brand around the journey.

title: Video editor needed for reels
proj_desc:
Video Editor — Editing Style & Ongoing Content Brief

I’m looking for a video editor to work with on an ongoing basis, primarily creating short-form content for social media.

I’ve included the Instagram page below as a reference for the editing style I’m looking for:



What I particularly like about their content is the overall editing style, pacing, transitions, visual effects, colour grading, text animation, sound design, and polished feel.

I’m looking for someone who can replicate that overall style as closely as possible rather than simply creating a generic “Reels/TikTok” edit.

The main adaptation

The one major difference is that I want to incorporate a talking-head video in the corner of the screen throughout the content.

The primary footage/content would remain the focus, with my talking head appearing as a secondary element — positioned and styled in a way that feels natural within the reference editing style.

I’d want the talking-head element to be integrated into the edit rather than simply looking like a webcam overlay. Things such as framing, masking, borders, shadows, movement, positioning and transitions should all feel intentional and consistent with the overall visual style.

What I’m looking for

Ideally, you would be comfortable with:

* Fast-paced, engaging short-form editing
* Replicating the reference page’s overall editing language
* Dynamic cuts and transitions
* Motion graphics and animated text
* Clean typography and on-screen captions
* Strong sound design and music selection
* Professional colour grading
* Subtle visual effects where appropriate
* Zooms, punch-ins and movement to maintain attention
* Integrating a talking-head element into the composition
* Creating edits that feel polished and premium rather than templated

Content volume

I’m looking to publish approximately 3–4 videos per week, so I’m interested in building an ongoing working relationship with the right editor rather than hiring for a one-off project.

Consistency is important to me, so once we establish the visual style, I’d want that style carried across every video.

What I’d like to know from you

Before moving forward, I’d like to know:

1. Is this style something you’re capable of replicating?
2. How closely can you match the editing, pacing, colour grading, transitions, text animation and overall visual style of the reference?
3. Are you comfortable incorporating a talking head in the corner while maintaining the same polished aesthetic?
4. Can you provide examples of similar work you’ve done?
5. What would your pricing look like for 3–4 videos per week?
6. What would your typical turnaround time be?
7. Would you be comfortable doing an initial test edit so I can see how closely you can match the reference?

The most important thing for me is quality and consistency. I’m not necessarily looking for the cheapest editor — I’m looking for someone who can genuinely achieve the visual standard I’m after and become a reliable long-term editing partner.

title: Animated App Explainer Video
proj_desc:
## Animated App Explainer Video – Nurture UAE

We are looking for a talented **motion graphics / animation designer** to create a short, professional explainer video for our childcare app, **Nurture UAE**.

### About Nurture

Nurture is an app designed to help parents and nannies/caregivers stay connected throughout a child's day.

Parents and caregivers can share daily care updates, communicate through the app and access tools including activities, meals & recipes, learning resources and more.

### What we want to create

We would like a **60–90 second animated explainer video** demonstrating how Nurture works.

The video will be narrated by our existing owl mascot, **Nuri**.

Nuri should become an animated character who **flies/moves around the screen, talks to the viewer and points towards different areas of the Nurture app interface** as they are being explained.

We will provide the original Nuri mascot artwork and access/screenshots/screen recordings of the app.

### Example flow

The video should demonstrate:

**1. Parent joins Nurture**

Nuri introduces the app while the Nurture interface appears on screen.

**2. Connecting a caregiver**

Show how a parent creates/connects their account and invites their nanny or caregiver to join their family.

Nuri flies alongside the interface and points towards the relevant buttons/actions.

**3. Daily Care**

Show how the nanny can record things such as:

• Meals
• Naps
• Activities
• Photos
• Mood/care updates

And how the parent can see these updates during their day.

**4. Messaging**

Demonstrate parent–caregiver messaging and Nurture's translation functionality.

**5. Activities**

Show the activity section and how caregivers can find age-appropriate activity ideas for the child.

**6. Meals & Recipes**

Briefly demonstrate the recipe/meal features available to caregivers.

**7. Nanny Learning**

Show the learning resources available to help caregivers build their knowledge and skills.

**8. Ending**

Bring Nuri back prominently on screen alongside Nurture branding and a simple CTA:

**Your child's day. All in one place.**

**Download Nurture UAE – available on the App Store & Google Play.**

### Style we're looking for

The finished video should feel **premium, modern, friendly and professional**.

Nuri should add personality and warmth, but we don't want the video to feel overly childish. The primary audience is **parents of young children in the UAE**.

We would particularly like someone who can combine:

• 2D character animation
• Motion graphics
• App/UI animation
• Screen recordings
• Professional transitions
• Voiceover/narration syncing
• Sound effects/background music

Nuri's existing design and colours **must remain consistent with our supplied mascot** rather than being redesigned or replaced with a generic AI-generated owl.

### Deliverables

• Final 60–90 second explainer video
• Vertical **9:16 version** for Instagram/Reels/TikTok
• Landscape **16:9 version** for website/YouTube
• High-resolution MP4 files
• Animated Nuri mascot
• Background music/sound design
• Subtitles/on-screen captions
• Source/project files where possible

We can provide the Nurture branding, mascot artwork, app screenshots/screen recordings and guidance on the features that need to be demonstrated.

### When applying

Please send examples of **app explainer videos, UI animations or character animation** you've previously created.

If possible, please also explain how you would approach animating our existing owl mascot alongside screen recordings of the Nurture app.

We're looking for someone who can take the concept and turn it into a polished, engaging video rather than simply assembling screenshots into a slideshow.

title: Music Lead Personalisation Writer
proj_desc:
I’m looking for reliable freelancers to research independent music artists for an Australian music marketing agency.

We’ll begin with a **paid trial of 50 accepted leads**. If the quality is strong, there is regular ongoing work available.

For ongoing work, you must be able to consistently complete **at least 50 accepted leads per week**.

### Artist criteria

Every artist must:

- Be based outside Australia
- Primarily come from English-speaking markets such as the US, UK, Canada, New Zealand or Ireland
- Have **10,000 Spotify monthly listeners or fewer**
- Have released qualifying music within the **last 6 months**
- Be an independent/emerging artist suitable for music marketing outreach
- Have a valid contact email
- Not already exist in our database
- Not be an AI-generated artist

Please use the artist’s **most recent qualifying release** wherever possible.

Instrumental-only artists/releases do not qualify.

### Each lead must include

- Artist name
- Artist country
- Contact email
- Link showing where the email was found
- Spotify artist link
- Spotify monthly listeners
- Recent song/release
- Release date
- Instagram or main social link
- Personalisation observation

A duplicate-checking tool will be provided. Every artist must be checked before being included in the final list.

### Personalisation

This is one of the most important parts of the role.

You must **genuinely listen to the selected song** and write a short observation about something specific you noticed or liked.

This could relate to:

- Vocals
- Melody
- Instrumentation
- Guitar or drum parts
- Production
- Arrangement
- Groove
- Hook
- Lyrics
- Dynamics

The personalisation does **not** need to be long. One accurate and specific observation is enough.

For example:

“Really liked how the guitars open up when the chorus comes in against the softer verse.”

Generic comments such as “Great song”, “Nice vocals” or “Love the vibe” will not be accepted.

Please also avoid automated technical audio-analysis comments involving BPM, EQ, frequencies, spectral analysis, etc.

If mentioning lyrics, please make sure the lyric genuinely belongs to that exact song. If you are unsure about a lyric, comment on another musical element instead.

I am primarily looking for **accuracy, genuine listening and reliability**. Perfect English or polished copywriting is not required.

### Trial and ongoing work

The initial project is for **50 accepted, non-duplicate leads**.

If the trial is successful, ongoing work is available in regular batches.

For ongoing work, you must be able to reliably complete **at least one 50-lead batch per week**. More work is available if you can consistently maintain quality at a higher volume.

### When applying

Please include **2–3 example personalisation comments based on real songs you have listened to**.

Please do not send generic examples. I want to see that you can listen to a song and identify a genuine, specific detail from it.

title: Node.js / TypeScript Dev for Browser Based MMO Game Backend
proj_desc:
I’m developing an MMORPG RTS, a browser based multiplayer strategy game.

The project is already in development and has an existing Node.js / TypeScript codebase and game engine.

I’m looking for an experienced developer to help continue the backend development. 

The game runs in a shared universe where players manage buildings and units, research technology, move fleets, fight other players and compete for territory. Actions continue to resolve while players are offline.

A core requirement of the game is deterministic, server authoritative simulation. Combat, movement, resource production and other game systems need to produce consistent results from the same inputs. 

The existing engine is structured as pure TypeScript and is shared between server side systems and the combat simulator.

The game specification is already extensive. It defines fleet movement, resource production, construction and research queues, combat, colonisation, espionage, player protection, territory, sensors and other systems. For example, fleet travel uses deterministic coordinates, ship speeds and technology modifiers, with the slowest ship determining fleet speed.

The work will involve:
- Working with the existing Node.js / TypeScript codebase
- Extending and completing backend game systems
- Implementing mechanics from an existing specification
- Maintaining deterministic game engine behaviour
- Working with persistent timed events, queues and fleet movements
- Integrating game-engine logic with the API/database where required
- Fixing bugs and inconsistencies in existing systems
- Writing or maintaining automated tests for important game rules
- Helping prepare the backend for multiplayer testing and eventual production use

This is not primarily a graphics/game engine role. The game is browser based and interface driven. I am specifically looking for someone strong in backend application architecture and TypeScript/Node.js.

Required experience:
- Strong Node.js and TypeScript
- Backend/API development
- Relational databases and data modelling
- Automated testing
- Git
- Ability to understand and work safely within an existing codebase
- Experience implementing business/game rules from written specifications
Experience with persistent multiplayer games, simulation systems, background workers/queues or server-authoritative game logic would be useful, but is not essential if your backend fundamentals are strong.

When applying, please answer these three questions:
1. Tell me about the most technically relevant Node.js/TypeScript project you have personally worked on. What parts did you implement?
2. How would you approach testing a deterministic game engine where identical inputs must always produce identical outputs?
3. Have you worked with systems involving scheduled/background processing, queues, timed events or persistent multiplayer state? If so, briefly explain.

Please don't send a generic agency introduction. I'm interested in the developer who would actually be working on the project.

I can provide:

* the complete script

* product visuals
* voice tracks if useful for production

**Before applying, please look carefully at the character reference images.**

Please send me one or two examples of work you have personally created that is genuinely relevant to this style, ideally involving dimensional or clay-like characters and character dialogue.

title: Business Start Up Guide Reviews
proj_desc:
Freelance Reviewer Wanted – Trade Business Start-Up Guides

Trade Skills Hub Academy (TSHA) is looking for freelancers to read and provide short, honest reviews of our practical business start-up guides for tradespeople and people considering starting their own small business.

The reviews will be published on the Trade Skills Hub Academy website to help potential readers understand what each guide contains and whether it may be useful to them.

The Work

You will be provided with a digital copy of one of our business start-up guides. Most guides are approximately 25,000–40,000 words, with an average length of around 30,000 words. You will receive the full digital guide and should read enough of it to provide a fair and informed review.

You will be asked to:

* Read enough of the guide to properly understand its content, structure and intended audience.
* Write a short, original review of approximately **100–150 words.
* Comment on areas such as:

  * How useful and practical the information is.
  * Whether the guide is easy to understand.
  * The range of topics covered.
  * Whether it would help someone considering starting that type of business.
  * Any particularly useful sections or features.
* Give your genuine opinion of the guides 

Important

We are not looking for artificially positive reviews.

Reviews should be fair, independent and honest. If you believe something could be improved, you are welcome to say so constructively.

The review must be based on actually reading the supplied guide and must not simply repeat the book description or marketing material.

Who We Are Looking For

You do not necessarily need to be a professional book reviewer.

We would particularly welcome applications from people with experience in:

* Running a small business.
* Self-employment.
* The construction or trade sectors.
* Business start-ups.
* Training, education or apprenticeships.
* Reviewing business or instructional publications.

Good written English and the ability to express an opinion clearly and concisely are essential.

Payment

This will be a fixed-price payment per completed review.

There are several TSHA business start-up guides available, so suitable freelancers may be offered additional titles.

A complimentary digital copy of each guide being reviewed will be supplied.

When Applying

Please briefly tell us:

1. Your relevant business, trade or reviewing experience.
2. Why you would be suitable for this work.
3. Your proposed fixed price per 100–150 word review.
4. Whether you would be interested in reviewing more than one guide.

Please include a short example of your writing if available.

Please note: These reviews are intended for the Trade Skills Hub Academy website. We are commissioning genuine editorial reviews, not purchasing positive ratings or customer reviews.

proj_desc:
We’re a UK-based company developing a website and digital platform specifically for radio stations, and we're looking for a talented web/UI designer to create five completely original, modern website themes for the platform.

This project is design only – no development/coding is required.

We want to create a collection of genuinely impressive website themes that radio stations can choose from and fully customise within our platform.

We don't want five variations of the same template. Each theme should have its own distinctive visual identity, layout and style, while still being practical enough to work as a real radio station website.

Think premium, modern, highly polished web design – strong typography, excellent use of space, creative layouts and a real "wow" factor.

We particularly want to avoid designs that look like generic WordPress templates, ThemeForest themes or obvious AI-generated concepts.

We'd initially like 5 complete theme concepts, covering the key pages and components a typical radio station would need, including:

- Homepage
- Schedule / radio shows
- Presenter/show profile
- News/article listing and article page
- Listen Live / player experience
- Contact/general content pages
- Reusable content components such as CTAs, cards, grids and promotional areas
- Responsive/mobile designs

The themes will also need to accommodate common radio-specific content such as Now Playing, Recently Played, On Air, Schedules, Presenters, News, Events, Competitions, Listen Live, Advertising and Social Content.

Our platform allows customers to customise colours, typography, imagery and content, so the designs need to work as flexible design systems rather than completely fixed websites.

We're specifically looking for a designer who can bring their own creative ideas to the project. The five designs should be visibly and structurally different, rather than simply changing colours, fonts and imagery.

For example, one could take a clean editorial approach, another could be bold and entertainment-led, another highly visual and contemporary, and another particularly suited to local/community broadcasting.

These are examples rather than prescribed creative directions – we'd like to see what you can come up with.

We'd ideally like designs supplied in Figma, including desktop and mobile layouts, reusable components, typography and colour systems, consistent spacing/grids, relevant interaction states, and any useful implementation notes for our developers.

The designs will be implemented separately by our own development team.

We're primarily interested in the quality of your portfolio and your ability to produce original UI design. Experience with media, entertainment, music, editorial or SaaS products would be useful, although previous radio industry experience isn't essential.

When applying, please include your portfolio, 2–3 particularly relevant examples, your proposed price for the project, estimated timescale, and a short explanation of how you'd approach making the five themes genuinely distinctive.

Please don't send a generic or AI generated proposal.

There is potential for ongoing work designing additional themes and other parts of the platform if we find the right designer.

Indicative budget: £750–£1,250 for the five-theme project. 

The first milestone will be the design of one complete theme, allowing us to establish the creative direction, design quality and how well the proposed design system will work within our platform.

Once the first theme is approved, we'll proceed with the remaining four themes as further milestones with the same designer.

title: Identity & Graphic Development.
proj_desc:
Project Description

We are looking for a graphic designer to professionally refine and develop an existing visual concept for Incessant Music, a UK music company.

This is not a logo redesign or website redesign. The website, brand identity and core visual direction already exist. We need a designer who can understand the concept we have developed and elevate its execution rather than replace it with a new design direction.

At the centre of the concept is a concentric-ring graphic derived from our existing brand mark. This graphic develops progressively across our five service areas, moving from one ring through to five rings.

Each of the five services has its own distinct colour, creating a recognisable visual identity for that service while remaining part of one connected system.

Ring Progression & Colour Hierarchy

The system progresses from one ring for Service 1 through to five rings for Service 5. As additional rings are introduced, they should not all inherit the service colour or become equally prominent.

In every service graphic, only the outermost ring carries the distinct colour assigned to that service.

The preceding inner rings — whether there are one, two, three or four — should remain extremely subtle, low-visibility and largely neutral/ghosted. Their purpose is to create a sense of progression, depth and continuity between the five services, not to compete visually with the coloured outer ring.

By Service 5, for example, the viewer should see one clearly defined coloured outer ring with four much more subdued rings sitting behind/within it.

Visual Direction

We want the ring system to have a sense of depth, dimension and atmosphere — almost suspended or floating within the space rather than simply sitting on a flat background.

We are interested in the sophisticated use of light, transparency, reflection, depth and subtle environmental illumination to achieve this.

The treatment should feel three-dimensional and atmospheric without becoming overly glossy or overpowering. The coloured outer ring should provide the principal visual energy, while the ghosted inner rings contribute depth and structure.

The finished direction should feel premium, contemporary, atmospheric, editorial and rooted in the music industry.

We are specifically not looking for a gaming, crypto, sci-fi or heavily neon aesthetic.

We are looking for someone with a strong eye for brand identity, composition and sophisticated digital graphics, who is comfortable developing an established creative direction rather than starting again.

References Supplied

We will provide:

Existing service-page concept — showing how the graphic system integrates with the website and demonstrating the 1–5 ring progression across the five services.
Ring treatment reference — demonstrating the type of dimensional, translucent/glass quality we are exploring.
Original Incessant Music vector brand mark (SVG) — showing the source of the concentric-ring visual language.
Atmosphere / depth reference — the blue floating-object image supplied with the project. This is provided only as a reference for atmosphere, spatial depth, environmental light and the feeling of an object suspended within a space. It is not a reference for the shape or design itself.

These references are intended to communicate the creative principles rather than prescribe the finished execution. We want the selected designer to bring their own professional judgement and creativity to how these qualities are achieved.

What We're Looking For

When responding, please include any examples of previous work demonstrating sophisticated digital graphics, brand-system development, dimensional graphic treatments or the refinement of an existing visual identity.

The successful designer should be able to look at the supplied material and recognise that the objective is to elevate and professionally execute an existing concept — not replace it with an unrelated new one.

title: Daylight & Sunlight Assessment
proj_desc:
Brief:
We need an independent daylight and sunlight assessment for a live planning application at Units 6, 7 and 8, Century Court, Tolpits Lane, Watford WD18 9RS (Three Rivers District Council, ref 26/1188/FUL). The scheme converts an existing two-storey commercial building (about 8.5 m high) to 26 flats and adds three storeys. The proposed parapet is 13.65 m and the top of the fourth-floor volume is 15.256 m, set back about 0.8 m from the parapet.
We have done a desktop 25° obstruction-angle check. We now need a proper 3D-modelled assessment to the BRE guide "Site Layout Planning for Daylight and Sunlight" (3rd edition, 2022), to submit to the council.
Scope: please model and report on:
1.	Ved House (also known as Unit 3 Century Court). This is residential and about 30–40 m north of the site. Please provide: 
o	VSC, NSL and APSH/WPSH (for windows facing within 90° of south) for the south-facing windows.
o	Existing against proposed, at the 15.256 m overall height.
o	A second run at the 13.65 m parapet for comparison.
2.	Neighbouring commercial units, Units 1, 2, 4 and 5 Century Court (5–10 m from the building). Please advise which have windows facing the site and whether the room uses give a reasonable expectation of daylight under the BRE guide. For those that do, run VSC and NSL, existing against proposed. We can supply what we know about the uses.
3.	Overshadowing. The 2-hours-of-sun-on-21-March test for any neighbouring amenity space, plus the communal gardens within the site if you recommend it.
4.	Optional quote line: internal daylight (ADF or the BRE 2022 illuminance method) for the proposed flats, priced separately so we can compare.
Please also tell us:
•	Your recommendation if any window falls below the BRE guide values, including any small design changes that would fix it. Our hand calculation puts the Ved House ground floor at 24.99° against the 25° limit, so we expect that result to be very tight.
•	What survey information or access you need (window positions, sill heights and so on).
We will provide:
•	The planning drawings: plans, elevations, sections and an OS block and location plan (PDF; DWG can follow on request).
•	Our existing desktop assessment with the 25° calculations.
Deliverable: a report in Word or PDF that is ready to submit to the council. It should include methodology, a model description, results tables for every window and room tested, drawings or plots, and a conclusion against the BRE criteria. It should also include a short statement we can hand to the planning officer if the council queries it.
